items.title: Anthropic ships Claude Meetings (beta): Claude joins your video call and builds the doc while you talk
items.summary: Claude joins a Google Meet call as a visible participant, listens, answers questions out loud or in chat, and co-builds docs, whiteboards, and other artifacts live with whoever is on the invite. After the call, notes, action items, and artifacts live on a per-meeting page, and users can add Claude to upcoming meetings from their calendar. Beta on Team and Enterprise plans, Google Meet only for now.
items.why: This turns Claude from something you paste meeting notes into afterward into something that is actually in the room doing the drafting while the conversation happens.
items.action: Add Claude to your next internal Google Meet (Team/Enterprise plan) and see what the live doc looks like by the time the call ends.

items.title: A Google engineer pairs Gemini with the Z3 solver to find Go bugs that go test -fuzz missed
items.summary: Google Developer Relations' Karl Weinmeister compiled his Go linter to see which runtime bounds-check traps survived the compiler's optimizer, then had Gemini 4 Argon translate each surviving trap into a Z3 constraint-solver model. Z3 found concrete crashing inputs in under a minute per function, and go test replayed them to confirm they were real. The pipeline caught 3 deliberately planted bugs plus 3 real latent bugs the existing fuzz suite had missed.
items.why: This is a genuinely different failure mode than asking an agent to find bugs: the LLM only translates assembly into solver constraints, and the solver, not the model, is what actually proves a crash is reachable.
items.action: Pick one Go function you are not fully sure is panic-safe and see what bounds-check traps the compiler's optimizer left behind before deciding whether the full pipeline is worth setting up.
